newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Treasury yields seen higher at next auction.
newsitem.headline: Spain Treasury yields seen higher at next auction.

text.p: The Spanish Treasury will likely pay higher yields at its monthly refunding this week, dealers said on Monday.
The new tranches of three-to-15 year notes and bonds are expected to be allotted at prices under current levels in the secondary market.
The market's uncertainty following a sharp fall in U.S. Treasuries prices was seen pushing prices down at the two-day Spanish refunding, dealers said.
The usual worries about European economic and monetary union were also weighing on the fixed-income market ahead of the auctions.
"These auctions hit the market at difficult times," a dealer in Madrid said.
"In theory, current secondary prices seem attractive. But the trend in the international markets suggests a more cautious approach," he added.
That caution is likely to push Spanish yields higher.
Earlier on Monday, the Spanish Treasury said it expects to issue a total of 425 billion pesetas at its regular monthly auction on Tuesday and Wednesday, with a maximum amount of 530 billion.
"I think the Treasury will have to pay a premium (over the secondary market)", said another dealer.
"In the past I would have considered these yields very attractive..But they are not so anymore with such high volatility in the international markets," he added.
Earlier on Monday, 6.75 percent three-year notes were trading in the market with a yield around 6.15 percent versus 5.922 percent at the auction at the beginning of March.
Five-year 7.90 percent notes were trading at around 6.50 percent versus 6.32 percent at the last auction, while 10-year 7.35 percent bonds were trading at 7.20 percent versus 6.929 percent.
The 15-year 8.70 percent bond was trading at around 7.43 percent on Monday versus 7.155 percent at the previous sale.
Dealers said the majority of new issuance is likely to be allotted in the three- and five-year maturities, where investor demand is expected to be strongest.
In the first quarter this year, the Spanish Treasury allotted 1.538 trillion pesetas in long-and-medium term notes and bonds, with 1.1 trillion in the three- and five-year sector.
Dealers said they were a bit surprised the Treasury had increased its total target allocation compared with March.

It increased the amount of notes and bonds it intends to sell to a minimum of 275 billion pesetas versus 250 billion pesetas for the three-and 10-year auction and to 150 billion from 125 billion for the five- and 15-year bonds.
